```{=html}
<div class="hero-banner">
  <div class="hero-eyebrow">LIGO Interferometer Precision Instrumentation</div>
  <h1 class="hero-title">
    Your sweep is wasting<br>
    <span class="hero-accent">90% of its measurement time.</span>
  </h1>
  <p class="hero-subtitle">
    A flat broadband injection spends drive power uniformly — the vast majority
    on frequencies where the model is already well-constrained.
    <strong style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.92);">system_ident</strong>
    runs the Pintelon–Schoukens method end to end: given a prior model and a fixed
    drive-power budget, it computes <em>exactly</em> where each Hz of bandwidth
    buys the most Fisher information, lays a low-crest periodic multisine there,
    measures the response <em>leakage-free</em>, fits the plant by
    <em>maximum likelihood</em> at the Cramér–Rao bound, and repeats — all with
    hardware-safe Tukey ramps and an operator STOP.
  </p>
  <div class="hero-ctas">
    <a href="tutorial/overview.html" class="btn btn-primary btn-lg">Understand the method</a>
    <a href="examples/01-single-resonance.html" class="btn btn-outline-light btn-lg">See it in action</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: true
#| warning: false
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance

# ── plant and prior ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
freq   = np.linspace(0.1, 4.0, 600)
model  = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)], gain=1.0)
Pyy    = np.ones_like(freq)
Px_tot = 1.0

Pxx_opt  = optimal_excitation(freq, model, Pyy, Px_tot, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
resp     = np.abs(model.eval(freq))

T_tot   = 256.0
cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, model, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, T_tot)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, model, Pxx_flat, Pyy, T_tot)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

# ── colour palette matching the site ───────────────────────────────────────
SKY  = '#1F8AC0'
GOLD = '#C8973A'
GRAY = '#94A3B8'
NAVY = '#0B2447'

fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1,
    shared_xaxes=True,
    row_heights=[0.42, 0.58],
    vertical_spacing=0.04,
)

# top panel — plant magnitude
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=resp,
    mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.5),
    name='|G(f)| — plant response',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.2f} Hz<br>|G| = %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>',
), row=1, col=1)

# bottom panel — optimal (filled)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_opt),
    mode='lines',
    fill='tozeroy',
    fillcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.18)',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.5),
    name=f'Optimal excitation  (var ratio: {ratio:.0f}×)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.2f} Hz<br>ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

# bottom panel — flat
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GRAY, width=1.8, dash='dash'),
    name='Flat sweep (equal total power)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.2f} Hz<br>ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

# resonance annotation on top panel
f0_idx = np.argmax(resp)
fig.add_annotation(
    x=freq[f0_idx], y=resp[f0_idx],
    xref='x', yref='y',
    text=f'<b>f₀ = 1 Hz, Q = 20</b>',
    showarrow=True, arrowhead=2, arrowsize=1.2,
    arrowcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.7)',
    ax=55, ay=-38,
    font=dict(size=11, color=GOLD, family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
    bgcolor='rgba(11,36,71,0.0)',
    bordercolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)',
    row=1, col=1,
)

# variance reduction annotation on bottom panel
fig.add_annotation(
    x=1.0, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_opt).max() * 0.55,
    xref='x2', yref='y2',
    text=f'<b>{ratio:.0f}× lower<br>parameter variance</b>',
    showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=12, color='rgba(200,151,58,0.9)', family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
    align='center',
    bgcolor='rgba(11,36,71,0.65)',
    bordercolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.3)',
    borderwidth=1,
    borderpad=6,
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white',
    height=460,
    margin=dict(l=55, r=25, t=18, b=50),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12, color='#1A2340'),
    legend=dict(
        orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02,
        xanchor='right', x=1,
        font=dict(size=11),
        bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.85)',
        bordercolor='#DCE5F0',
        borderwidth=1,
    ),
    plot_bgcolor='#FFFFFF',
    paper_bgcolor='#FFFFFF',
)

fig.update_yaxes(
    title_text='|G(f)|',
    type='log', row=1, col=1,
    gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',
    linecolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.15)',
)
fig.update_yaxes(
    title_text='Drive ASD  [1/√Hz]',
    row=2, col=1,
    gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',
    linecolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.15)',
)
fig.update_xaxes(
    title_text='Frequency  [Hz]',
    row=2, col=1,
    gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',
    linecolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.15)',
)
fig.update_xaxes(
    gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',
    row=1, col=1,
)

fig.show()
```

<div class="page-section">
  <p class="section-label">Why it works</p>
  <div class="feature-grid">

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#119979;</span>
      <h3>Fisher-optimal excitation</h3>
      <p>The dispersion function ν(f) tells you how much each frequency bin contributes to
         parameter information given the current drive and readout noise.
         The Pintelon–Schoukens fixed-point iteration redistributes drive power toward
         high-ν bins under a fixed total-power budget — converging to the optimal spectrum
         in 3–5 iterations.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#128257;</span>
      <h3>Leakage-free measurement, ML fit</h3>
      <p>The periodic multisine makes the response DFT leakage-free — a sharp resonance is
         measured at its true peak with no near-resonance bias. A reference-based,
         ratio-of-averages FRF cancels the controller in closed loop, and the Gaussian
         maximum-likelihood estimator turns it into model parameters at the Cramér–Rao
         bound. Passes accumulate by inverse-variance weighting, so broadband coverage is
         never thrown away, only enriched.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#9741;</span>
      <h3>Hardware-safe injection</h3>
      <p>The multisine carries low-crest <strong>Schroeder phases</strong>, so a
         saturation-limited actuator delivers the most in-band power for a fixed peak.
         Every waveform is Tukey-windowed (configurable ramp), keeping the actuation
         envelope within budget at startup and teardown. The watchdog monitors actuator
         and RMS levels every read segment; a breach or operator STOP triggers an
         immediate safe handoff.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#9881;</span>
      <h3>Same API — twin or hardware</h3>
      <p>The loop code never sees actuator channels or frame data directly — it speaks
         a backend abstraction. <code>TwinBackend</code> runs the full campaign on a
         digital plant model at development time; swapping in the CDS backend is a
         single config line, no code changes.</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>

<div class="page-section">
  <p class="section-label">Get started</p>
  <h2 style="font-family:'Outfit',sans-serif; font-size:1.6rem; font-weight:700; margin-bottom:1rem;">
    Run a full campaign in 60 seconds
  </h2>
  <p>Install into your environment, then run the digital-twin demo that exercises the
     full POS/PIT/YAW suspension campaign:</p>

  <div class="quickstart-block">
    <span class="qs-comment"># install (from the repo root)</span><br>
    <span class="qs-prompt">$ </span>pip install -e ".[dev]"<br>
    <br>
    <span class="qs-comment"># run the twin demo — no hardware required</span><br>
    <span class="qs-prompt">$ </span>system_ident run src/system_ident/configs/twin_demo.yml --twin --yes<br>
    <span class="qs-output">DONE (target reached); per-DoF fractional uncertainty ~1e-9</span><br>
    <br>
    <span class="qs-comment"># or drive it from Python</span><br>
    <span class="qs-prompt">$ </span>python<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span><span class="qs-keyword">from</span> system_ident.config <span class="qs-keyword">import</span> RunConfig<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span><span class="qs-keyword">from</span> system_ident.loop   <span class="qs-keyword">import</span> SysIDLoop<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span>rc = RunConfig.load(<span class="qs-string">"src/system_ident/configs/twin_demo.yml"</span>)<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span>backend = rc.build_twin_backend(seed=0)<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span>loop = SysIDLoop(backend, rc.build_estimator(),<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">... </span>                rc.build_designer(), rc.build_watchdog(backend))<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span>result = loop.run(rc.raw, rc.build_priors(), seed=0)<br>
    <span class="qs-keyword">&gt;&gt;&gt; </span>result.done<br>
    <span class="qs-output">True</span>
